newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen stable to soft, supplies ample.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen stable to soft, supplies ample.

text.p: Ample supplies were expected to offset any gains in paper quotes to nudge high sulphur fuel oil prices lower, traders said on Monday.
Traders said fuel oil swaps were firmer as buying interest were strong. Bids/Offers on Monday were quoted at $118.50/$119.50, up from Friday's quotes at $117/$117.75.
The firm paper quotes have also sparked off higher offers in the bunker market as bunker traders said sentiment was firm.
Discussion were still heard that a local trader may be interested to see higher prices.
But most traders agree that the market remained long and there are no lack of supplies to meet demand.
Late Monday, an offer was seen by a major at $117 per tonne for end November loading supplies.
Quotes for 180cst cargoes loading in November was at $116-$118 per tonne on Friday.
Traders said some support may be seen from India which had issued a third tender in November to buy 14,000 tonnes of fuel oil.
On the SIMEX fuel oil futures, December was traded for the first time since August 1995 at $119.50 per tonne. Only 10 lots changed hands.
Traders said the levels were indicative of current market fundamentals.
